summary: Researched just after midnight on Mon 16 Nov and re-checked this morning with live prices; lineups are not out, so this is a draft until the final check. It is the last Nations League matchday, so every game was checked first for a favourite with nothing left to play for. Eight games were researched: three are kept at medium, two at low and three are excluded. No favourite's price fell overnight. Medium: Iceland–Luxembourg (p 0.775; Iceland need a point for promotion, Luxembourg have lost four straight without scoring; Iceland lose Hordur (suspended), Stefan Teitur and Kristall Mani (injured), the forecast wind and sleet have eased), Lithuania–Liechtenstein (p 0.87; the coach reports a fit squad, Kucys suspended; Liechtenstein have not scored in the group), Slovenia at North Macedonia (p 0.62; Slovenia need the win for second place, North Macedonia are relegated with one goal in five games; Slovenia are without Bijol and Sesko). Low, so not bet: Greece–Serbia (Serbia's absentees and XI are now verified, but Greece have no probable XI after the 0-7 loss), Medvedev–Cobolli (no second bookmaker price; tennis now needs high anyway). Excluded: Switzerland–Scotland and Gibraltar–Malta (the favourite has already won its group and the opponent still needs the result; both prices fell 3–5%), Germany–Netherlands (fierce rivalry, near coin flip). Final check (about 16:05 UTC): the lineups for both 17:00 games are on ESPN. Iceland start an attacking 4-3-3 (Oskarsson, Gudjohnsen, Willumsson) with Hjortur and Victor Palsson covering the suspended Hordur, and the price has risen 6% since first listing; Lithuania play a cautious 5-3-2 with Ruzgis up front, and Liechtenstein, who have not scored in five games, drifted further. Neither lineup is confirmed by its federation, so both stay medium; the under-3.5 view for Iceland is shaded down because a heavy home win is the main risk. Evening check for the 19:45 games (19:12 UTC): Greece–Serbia raised to medium after a strong Greek XI; Slovenia stays medium with a weakened XI.

checks.team_news: New today: no new injury or illness news found. The ESPN summary (event 401861184) now lists a Lithuania XI, with all names from the squad Cepas had named. Kucys is out through suspension; Ruzgis is in his place up front. Morning findings still hold: Cepas said all players are fit, and Liechtenstein reported a fully fit squad (GK Oehri back from an ACL injury). I found no Liechtenstein report from lfv.li or Vaterland and no late news from LFF, LRT or 15min.
checks.lineups: Lithuania (ESPN, 5-3-2): GK Voitinovicius; Gineitis, Sluta, Tutyskinas, Sirvys, Jankauskas, Dolznikov, Lasickas, Burba, Ruzgis, Kazukolovas. That is a back-five shape with Ruzgis in attack and Voitinovicius in goal rather than Bartkus. The ESPN list gives no positions beyond the keeper, so it is not a verified official XI, and I could not confirm it against LFF or LRT. Liechtenstein: no XI found anywhere (ESPN roster empty), so I do not know whether they picked a more attacking side than the expected 5-4-1 and could not check their strikers or shape. Searches (Sofascore, Sports Mole, starting11) only gave predicted XIs and the September fixture.
checks.rotation: The Lithuania XI looks like a settled, defensive-minded side. I did not check how many changes there are against the Suriname game. Liechtenstein's changes are unknown, since no XI is out.
checks.motivation: Unchanged. Lithuania need a point for 2nd place; Liechtenstein have nothing realistic to play for. Cepas is in his second match as interim coach.
checks.form: Lithuania scored only 3 goals in 3 group games and drew 0-0 with Suriname despite many chances. Liechtenstein have scored 0 in all three group games and in their last five matches, and have 1W 1D 13L in their last 15. This supports BTTS no.
checks.h2h: Lithuania won 2-0 away on 24 Sep 2026, and the last three meetings were all 2-0 Lithuania wins. Liechtenstein did not score in any of them.
checks.odds: Live Polymarket: Lithuania 88.5%, draw 9.4%, Liechtenstein 2.1%. First listed 87.5 / 9.5 / 3.1, so Lithuania has firmed about 1 point, with no adverse move. BTTS no is now 83% live, up from 78% when first listed. DraftKings via ESPN is 1.08 / 8 / 29 (opening 1.08 / 9 / 21), with a total line of 2.5. Liechtenstein have drifted out, which fits a low chance of them scoring. Stake and Rainbet prices: none seen.
checks.models: Elo (eloratings.net): Lithuania 1280 v Liechtenstein 882, expected score 0.946. Squawka projects 2-0 and Sports Mole 3-0, both Lithuania wins to nil.
checks.venue_weather: Darius and Girenas Stadium, Kaunas, kick-off 17:00 UTC. Cold, with a strong wind and possible light rain, which would slightly lower the goal count.

games.reason: For BTTS no (loses only if both teams score), the evidence is consistent. Liechtenstein have scored 0 goals in their last five matches, and in all three group games and the September meeting they did not score. Lithuania lined up in a 5-3-2, which points to a cautious side, and their price has firmed with no adverse news. BTTS no sits at 83% on the market. I put the view slightly under that at 79%, because the Liechtenstein XI is unconfirmed (I could not rule out a more attacking side than the expected 5-4-1) and a single goal from a set piece or counter would sink the leg. Confidence stays medium: the Lithuania XI is shown by ESPN but not verified against an official source, and the Liechtenstein XI is unknown. The views on Liechtenstein +2.5 and under 3.5 sit a little below their market prices. The -1.5 and over 1.5 legs get no view.
games.main_risk: Liechtenstein score once, for instance from a set piece or counter, while Lithuania score several, which would turn BTTS no into a loss. The unseen Liechtenstein XI could also hide a more attacking selection. A Lithuania win by 3 or more would sink Liechtenstein +2.5.

checks.team_news: New today: ESPN summary (event 401861182) now shows both starting XIs. Iceland start Hakon Valdimarsson (GK), Logi Tomasson, Hjortur Hermannsson, Victor Palsson and Daniel Gretarsson in defence, with Isak Johannesson, Mikael Ellertsson and Hakon Haraldsson in midfield. Orri Oskarsson, Andri Gudjohnsen and Brynjolfur Willumsson lead the attack. Hjortur and Victor Palsson cover for the suspended Hordur, which matches the morning's prediction. Gylfi Sigurdsson, Arnor Sigurdsson, Jon Dagur, Aron Gunnarsson and Brynjar Ingi are on the bench. Luxembourg start Anthony Moris (GK), Carlson, Mahmutovic, Selimovic, De Pina, Moreira, Olesen, Bohnert, Jans, Vincent Thill and Videira. The XIs come from ESPN only. I did not confirm them on KSI, fotbolti.net or Visir, and no late injury news was found. No Luxembourg weakness beyond the already known Natami suspension.
checks.lineups: ESPN lists Iceland in a 4-3-3 with three attackers (Orri, Gudjohnsen, Brynjolfur) and Luxembourg in a 3-1-4-2 with Vincent Thill and Videira up front. Iceland's XI is attack-minded, with Gylfi and Arnor held back on the bench. The back four is makeshift, with Hjortur and Victor Palsson at centre-back for the suspended Hordur. Luxembourg's goalkeeper is Moris, their usual number one. Official federation confirmation not seen.
checks.rotation: No heavy rotation. The changes come from the suspension and injuries (Hordur, Stefan Teitur, Kristall Mani), not from choice. Nothing in the XI suggests a rested side.
checks.motivation: Unchanged. Iceland need a point or a win for the group and promotion. Luxembourg are playing for pride.
checks.odds: Live Polymarket Iceland win is 0.8236 (draw 0.1326, away 0.0438), up from 0.7765 first listed. DraftKings via ESPN is now 1.17 (-600) / 6.5 (+550) / 15 (+1400), against -320 / +400 / +750 at the open. The total stays at 2.5, over -140 and under +110. The rise is explained by the confirmed strong, attacking Iceland XI. It runs in the favourite's favour. It also makes a 4+ goal game somewhat more likely, but the 2.5 line has hardly moved. The live Under 3.5 is 0.705 against 0.665 first listed, so that leg's price has risen, not fallen. Stake and Rainbet not seen.
checks.models: World Football Elo: Iceland 1632, Luxembourg 1359, expected score for Iceland 0.895. Consistent with the market.
checks.venue_weather: Unchanged from the morning: Laugardalsvollur, about -4C, light wind, no precipitation, pitch fine.
checks.form: Unchanged. Iceland: 1-1 Estonia, 3-0 at Luxembourg, 3-0 Bulgaria, 0-0 at Estonia, 5-0 at Bulgaria, with one goal conceded in five games. Luxembourg: four straight defeats without scoring (0-3 Iceland, 0-1 Estonia, 0-2 Bulgaria, 0-1 Estonia) after a 2-1 win at Bulgaria. Both Iceland draws came against Estonia. (unchanged from the morning check)
checks.h2h: Unchanged. Iceland won 3-0 in Luxembourg on 29 Sept 2026. Luxembourg have only two wins against Iceland (3-1 in Sept 2023 is the other), and none away. (unchanged from the morning check)

games.reason: The official-looking XIs (ESPN) show a strong, attacking Iceland side at home against a weak Luxembourg that has lost four straight without scoring, and the market has moved up to 82% for Iceland. I sit a little under the market (80%) because the XI is not confirmed on federation sources and the back line is makeshift. For Under 3.5, the attacking 4-3-3 and a Luxembourg 3-1-4-2 raise the chance of a lopsided score a little, so I shade the view below the live 0.705 to 0.67. The DraftKings total of 2.5 has not moved, which supports a low-scoring game as the central case.
games.main_risk: A heavy home win. Iceland's attacking XI against a weak Luxembourg could produce 4+ goals, which would lose the Under 3.5 leg. A makeshift Iceland back line could also concede.

checks.team_news: Neither is out. Cobolli (No.5 seed, Finals debut) retired in tears in Vienna R2 trailing Berrettini 5-2 in the 1st set; scans showed a minor left-leg muscle strain and he skipped the Paris Masters (tennismajors, flashscore). Per tennisworlditalia/tennisitaliano he says the injury is behind him and he trained at the Fan Village on Sunday with no visible problems, but I found no match played since the Vienna retirement. Medvedev (No.4 seed) had no injury reported; he said he was 'a bit tired' in Almaty in October. Sinner is out (knee), so the Finals field is not the original one. Alcaraz, the other group favourite, had a stomach issue and knee worries in practice. De Minaur and Fritz are alternates and nothing says either was called in.
checks.lineups: Order of play confirmed by Tennis Majors and tennistale: Mon 16 Nov, Inalpi Arena, Turin. Alcaraz v Tiafoe at 2pm CET; Medvedev v Cobolli is the night session, not before 8:30pm CET (19:30 UTC), matching the listed start. One search snippet claimed a Tuesday slot but the official order of play says Monday. No withdrawal or walkover announced.
checks.rotation: This is the first round-robin match for both. ATP group standings page shows all four Lendl Group players at no record yet. Medvedev's last event, the Paris Masters, ended with a 6-4 6-4 R2 loss to Buse on 4 Nov, so he has had about 11 days of rest. Cobolli has played nothing since the Vienna retirement (late Oct), so he comes in with match rust. Medvedev also played a heavy autumn: Almaty, Vienna, Paris. Next matches in the group are Alcaraz and Tiafoe.
checks.motivation: Group table before the game: all four 0-0 (Alcaraz, Medvedev, Cobolli, Tiafoe), so both players still have everything to play for. Top two go to the semi-finals, and a loss here leaves a player needing wins against Alcaraz and Tiafoe. No dead-rubber risk. Cobolli has the home crowd and high motivation in Turin.
checks.form: Medvedev: 3 titles this season and the most hard-court wins on tour (tennismajors, Oct). He went 11-1 in China, winning Hangzhou and reaching the Beijing SF, then lost the Shanghai SF to Jodar. He also played Almaty and Vienna, whose results I could not verify, then lost to Buse 6-4 6-4 in Paris R2 on 4 Nov. Cobolli: a strong season with a Roland Garros final run, qualifying for Turin for the first time; he beat Medvedev in Madrid in April, retired v Berrettini in Vienna, and withdrew from Paris. I could not retrieve a full last-10 list for either player (Tennis Abstract pages returned no data), so form is only partly verified.
checks.h2h: Medvedev leads 2-1 (tennismylife, ATP draw page). Medvedev won Beijing 2024 QF 6-2 6-4 (hard) and US Open 2024 R32 6-3 6-4 6-3 (hard). Cobolli won Madrid R16 on 29 Apr 2026 on clay, 6-3 5-7 6-4. Both Medvedev wins were on hard courts, the surface in Turin (indoor hard). Medvedev's baseline-counterpunching game suits fast indoor hard, while Cobolli's heavy forehand and movement make rallies physical.
checks.odds: The only second bookmaker price I found for this fixture is not for the Finals. Dimers and Oddschecker had Medvedev -120 / Cobolli +105 for the April Madrid match (Dimers sim 54.7/45.3), which is old and on clay. data.odds with DraftKings/ESPN is absent for this game, so I have no current second-bookmaker price. Polymarket 76% Medvedev; 24h move 0.765 to 0.760 (relative -0.7%), so there is no price drop to explain. De-vig not possible without a current second price.
checks.models: Tennis Abstract Elo (data.rating, tennisabstract.com/reports/atp_elo_ratings.html): Medvedev 1989.4 (hard 1960.6) vs Cobolli 1872.5 (hard 1797.2). Win probability for Medvedev: 66.2% overall, 71.9% hard, 69.1% blended. The bookmaker-free model sits 7 points below the Polymarket 76%, so I lower p to 0.72.
checks.venue_weather: Inalpi Arena, Turin, indoor hard court, best-of-three tie-break sets, so no weather risk. The crowd is strongly pro-Cobolli (Italian, debut at home), and the pace is fast, which suits Medvedev. Cobolli's Elo is much weaker on hard than overall.

games.reason: Medvedev is the sensible favourite: higher Elo on hard (about 69-72%), 2-1 head-to-head with both wins on hard, and Cobolli returning from a muscle strain with no match since Vienna. But confidence is low because the brief requires a verified second bookmaker price and a verified recent form list, and I found neither: there is no current non-Polymarket price for this match and no last-10 results for either player. Medvedev also lost early in Paris and Cobolli beat him in April.
games.main_risk: Cobolli wins in front of a home crowd, since his minor leg strain may have healed (he says it is behind him) and he beat Medvedev most recently in Madrid; Medvedev is also coming off a flat Paris loss and a long autumn. Opening group match nerves and a short best-of-three make an upset more plausible. Missing second price and incomplete form data keep confidence at low.

checks.team_news: Updated this morning. Greece: Kourbelis is out (Sport24). Ioannidis is also absent (Gazzetta). Tzolis is available. Saliakas and Zafeiris were suspended for the Dutch game and are back. No other injuries were reported. Serbia: Zivkovic and Dragojevic are confirmed out for the red cards against Germany (B92, Mozzart, Novosti), and Dragojevic has been sent to the U21s. Vlahovic is confirmed out. Pavlovic, Terzic, Kostic and Stankovic were already out (Novosti). Milenkovic IS in this squad and is expected to start. Mitrovic is not named in either Serbian article I read, so his status is unverified. Greek press speaks of seven Serbian absentees, which I did not verify. Lukic and Maksimovic return from suspension. Paunovic is back on the bench. The 0-7 loss is confirmed by the Greek press.
checks.lineups: Official XIs (ESPN, 18:45 UTC): Greece 4-2-3-1 Mandas; Rota, Mavropanos, Koulierakis, Tsimikas; Zafeiris, Androutsos; Karetsas, Tzolis, Pavlidis; Douvikas: a strong, not rotated side. Serbia 4-4-2 Petrovic; Erakovic, Milenkovic, Babic, Bukinac; Lukic, Milinkovic-Savic, Maksimovic, Nedeljkovic; Mitrovic, Jovic.
checks.rotation: Greece play three days after the 0-7 loss, and Gazzetta expects changes in defence, midfield and attack. Jovanovic said the team has the right pride to react and would not accept the favourite's role. Serbia are rested in midfield (Lukic and Maksimovic return) but lose Zivkovic and Dragojevic and have changes at the back (Erakovic in for Gudelj) and in goal (Petrovic).
checks.motivation: Table taken from last night (Netherlands 11, Germany 8, Greece 8, Serbia 0). I did not re-verify it this morning, and no article I read covered it or the Germany-Netherlands game at the same time. Greece still need a result. Serbia are on 0 points and say they play for pride (Paunovic). The stadium is sold out (about 23,000).
checks.form: Unchanged. Greece: W 2-1 at Serbia, W 1-0 vs Germany, D 2-2 and L 0-7 vs the Netherlands. Serbia: 0 points from 5.
checks.h2h: Greece 2-1 Serbia in Belgrade on 24 Sep 2026 (Douvikas 90+5).
checks.odds: Live Polymarket: Greece 68.3%, draw 19.3%, Serbia 12.4%. Greece were 67.3% when first listed, so the move is about +1 point. The 24h move is 67.5% to 68.5%. DraftKings is 1.42 / 4.50 / 6.50, opening 1.43, de-vig 65.2/20.5/14.2. The small drift towards Greece fits Serbia's suspensions and is not unexplained. My p is below the market on Greece because of the unconfirmed XI and the 0-7 hangover.
checks.models: Elo: Greece 1788, Serbia 1662, expected score 0.786. This is in line with the market.
checks.venue_weather: Panthessaliko Stadium, Volos, Greece's home ground. The Serbian press says it is sold out. No weather check.

games.reason: Fixture and kick-off confirmed (21:45 Greek time, 19:45 UTC). New this morning: Serbia's absentees and probable XI are verified, with Zivkovic, Dragojevic and Vlahovic out and Milenkovic playing. Greece have no probable XI yet, with only candidates and expected changes after the 0-7 loss. Mitrovic's status is not confirmed. Confidence stays low because the Greek XI is unknown and one Serbian absentee is unchecked. The market move since listing is small and explained. Final check (19:12 UTC): the Greek XI is out and strong (Pavlidis, Tzolis, Karetsas, Mavropanos, Tsimikas), Serbia are without Zivkovic, Dragojevic and Vlahovic, and the price has not fallen (0.673 to 0.687), so the game is raised to medium.
games.main_risk: Greece's unknown XI after the 0-7 loss, which means rotation, morale and a leaky defence, so a draw or one-goal win is the main risk. Serbia have little to lose and have scored 4 in 5. Against that, Serbia's weakened squad and the sold-out home crowd favour Greece.

games.reason: Hard rule: the favourite has nothing left to play for and the opponent still does. Group D1 is a three-team group. Sky Sports table (updated 15 Nov 21:48): Malta P3 W2 D1 L0 GF4 GA2 Pts7; Andorra P4 W1 D1 L2 GF3 GA3 Pts4 (finished); Gibraltar P3 W0 D2 L1 GF1 GA3 Pts2. This is the last match for Malta and Gibraltar (round 6). Malta (7 pts) cannot be caught, because Andorra max 4, so their group win is secured whatever happens. Gibraltar can still finish second above Andorra (a win gives 5 pts, a draw 3), so they still need a result and Malta do not. The Europa Point Stadium venue is Gibraltar's regular home ground, so it is not an exclusion reason. Malta's price also slid 66.5% to 64.5% (-3% relative) in 24h, and DraftKings moved from 1.43 to 1.49, with no news found to explain it. Lineups are not out, and no squad or injury news was found for either side. I could not confirm what second place is worth, but that does not change the dead-rubber verdict for the favourite.
games.main_risk: Malta already secured the group, so a rotated or unmotivated Malta side faces a Gibraltar side with something to gain. The first meeting finished 1-1, and the draw is priced at about 24%. Gibraltar have drawn 2 of their 3 games.

checks.team_news: Morning re-check, nothing new since last night. Slovenia: Jaka Bijol suspended (second yellow v Switzerland, RTV SLO, Planet Nogomet); Cesar's Sunday press conference gave no named replacement ('appropriate replacement' from the squad, decided at tactical training, Planet Nogomet); FotMob predicted XI lists Oblak in goal with Drkusic, Zec, Zaletel, Karnicnik in defence and Bijol unavailable (prediction only). David Brekalo still doubtful with an injury, no update found; Timi Max Elsnik and Jure Balkovec out; Sesko left out of the squad (24ur); Erik Janza and David Zec back from suspension. Oblak is in the squad, no fitness concern reported. North Macedonia: only Dimitar Mitrovski has a minor knock (Ekipa.mk, Sedloski press conference); no suspensions or new absences reported this morning. Slovenia missing Bijol and Sesko remains a soft risk.
checks.lineups: Official XIs (ESPN, 18:45 UTC): Slovenia 4-4-2 Oblak; Drkusic, Zec, Zaletel, Janza; Karnicnik, Gnezda Cerin, Lovric, Sturm; Vipotnik, Matko (new centre-back pair, no Sesko). North Macedonia 4-3-2-1 Dimitrievski; Ilievski, Musliu, Mladenovski, Alioski; Gashtarov, Bardhi, Elezi; Elmas, Churlinov; Rastoder.
checks.rotation: No rotation risk found. Slovenia chase second place and Cesar asks maximum effort from starters and substitutes (Planet Nogomet). 3-day turnaround after Switzerland (0-0, 13 Nov); last matchday, so nothing after it to save players for. North Macedonia are relegated with no next fixture affecting this game. No new overnight story on squad changes.
checks.motivation: Group B1 before this game: Switzerland 13 pts (group won), Slovenia 8, Scotland 7, North Macedonia 0 (relegated to League C). Switzerland v Scotland is played the same day. A Slovenia win gives 11 pts, which Scotland (max 10) cannot match, so second place and the promotion play-off are secured. A draw (9 pts) is enough only if Scotland fail to beat Switzerland. Slovenia have everything to play for; North Macedonia play for pride and a first win. The dead-rubber rule does not apply.
checks.form: Slovenia Nations League: L W D W D (5 goals for, 3 against), last game 0-0 v Switzerland; conceded in all three away games. North Macedonia: 5 straight Nations League defeats, 1 goal scored and 12 conceded, no win in 13 games in all competitions. Sources point to a low-scoring game (freetips.com and Football Whispers tip under 2.5). No xG found.
checks.h2h: Reverse fixture 29 Sep in Ljubljana: Slovenia 2-0 (Lovric, Matko). Slovenia have lost just one of the last five meetings. Main danger is a draw against a deep block; Slovenia's 0-0 with Switzerland shows they can fail to score.
checks.odds: Live Polymarket Slovenia 64.3% (home 12.4%, draw 23.3%), up from 62.5% last night (24h move +2.0 points, +3.2% relative, in the favourite's favour) and from 62.7% when first listed (p_first away 0.627, now 0.643). DraftKings via ESPN: home 6.50, draw 3.90, away 1.50, de-vigged 14.3% / 23.8% / 61.9%; opening away 1.61, so the book has also shortened Slovenia from 1.61 to 1.50. Total line 2.5. The small move is not tied to any news found (no new team-news story); it fits the steady drift toward the favourite. Draw no bet Slovenia live 87.7% (first listed 86.4%).
checks.models: World Football Elo: North Macedonia 1527, Slovenia 1726, expected score for the home side 0.361 (draw counts half), a smaller Slovenia edge than the market implies after the draw share. Statz had Slovenia 51% / North Macedonia 21%. Models are less bullish than the 64% market, so p is trimmed to 62% Slovenia.
checks.venue_weather: Tose Proeski National Arena, Skopje, 19:45 UTC (20:45 local), a normal home ground. Fog and about 8C forecast last night; no pitch or extreme weather problem reported.

games.reason: Slovenia are clear favourites (Elo 1726 v 1527, market 62-64%) and need the win to lock up second place; North Macedonia are relegated with 0 points and 1 goal in 5 games. This morning's re-check found no new negative news: Bijol still out with no confirmed replacement, Brekalo still doubtful, Oblak available, North Macedonia clean apart from Mitrovski's minor knock. The price moved slightly toward Slovenia without a visible news cause. The Slovenia draw-no-bet leg only loses if North Macedonia win (about 12-14% by market and book), and a draw is a push. Held at medium because Slovenia lack Bijol and Sesko, scored only 5 goals in 5 games, and the XI is unconfirmed.
games.main_risk: A North Macedonia win is the only way draw no bet loses, which needs a blunt Slovenia (no Sesko, a changed centre-back pairing without Bijol, possible Brekalo absence) to concede to a side that plans to attack more; a draw only voids the leg. For the other legs, a 0-0 or 1-1 or a one-goal Slovenia win hurts match-winner and handicap legs. The confirmed XI is weakened: a new centre-back pair and no Sesko against a full-strength North Macedonia.

games.reason: Hard rule: the favourite has nothing left to play for and the opponent still does. The ESPN Nations League standings, before this game, put Group B1 at: Switzerland P5 W4 D1 L0 GD +10, 13 pts; Slovenia P5 W2 D2 L1 GD +2, 8 pts; Scotland P5 W2 D1 L2 GD -1, 7 pts; North Macedonia P5 L5 GD -11, 0 pts. Switzerland can no longer be caught: Slovenia can reach 11 and Scotland 10, so Switzerland have already won the group and promotion to League A. Scotland are third, one point behind Slovenia. They still need a result to take second place and the promotion-playoff spot, so they have something to play for. The group's last matchday is on 16 Nov. Sources disagree on the exact table and on the playoff format. One preview lists Scotland on 4 pts, but the ESPN data matches Switzerland's 0-0 draw in Slovenia on 13 Nov and was used. I could not confirm whether second place or third place goes to the playoffs. Switzerland's 5.3% Polymarket price fall in 24h (0.565 to 0.535) and DraftKings' move from 1.67 to 1.77 also fit a side with nothing at stake. Another reason not to back Switzerland.
games.main_risk: Switzerland, already group winners and promoted, may rotate or ease off in a dead rubber, while Scotland need the result for the playoff spot. The Portugal 1-4 Denmark pattern applies.

games.reason: Hard rule: a fierce rivalry. Germany v Netherlands is one of international football's best-known rivalries, and the rules exclude derbies and fierce rivalries whatever the table says. It is also close to a coin flip: the market has Germany at about 50%, World Football Elo rates the Netherlands higher (1990 v 1916) and the first meeting this season finished 1-1. Germany are without Musiala and Gnabry, the Netherlands without Van Dijk and De Jong.
games.main_risk: A draw or Dutch win. The Netherlands are higher on Elo (1990 v 1916), unbeaten this season and strong after the 7-0, and the first meeting finished 1-1. A tight, cagey rivalry game with a Germany side missing Musiala and Gnabry would end level, and Opta gives the draw 26.8%. Lineups are unconfirmed.
